primarySubject: A reconstructed Reichsburg on the Sonnenberg above Annweiler, presented as a sandstone castle on a rock ridge.
definingSilhouette: A compact elevated fortress silhouette with one visually dominant main tower and subordinate wall/tower/building masses following the rocky ridge.
dominantTowerArrangement: Preserve the dominant main tower and the subordinate towers/structures exactly as seen in the approved viewpoint. Do not synthesize a generic castle tower count.
roofTypes: View-dependent and reference-led. Preserve only rooflines visible in approved references; do not add stereotypical conical roofs or invented caps.
relativeBuildingHeights: The main tower rises clearly above the lower ring-wall, gate and palas-related masses; the exact proportions follow the selected reference view.
architecturalMasses: Ring wall, gate way, fountain tower, main tower and the base of the palas are the named structural masses. The current appearance includes later historicizing additions.
facadeFeatures: Stone/sandstone masonry and the recognizable main-tower mass are essential. Preserve visible masonry rhythm without inventing windows, ornaments or crests.
terrainContext: The castle sits on the Sonnenberg above Annweiler in a forested Pfälzerwald/Trifelsland setting and is associated with a rock ridge.
foregroundBackground: Use a restrained rocky/wooded elevated context from an approved view. Annweiler and the wider landscape may support recognition but must not overpower the castle.
recognizableViewpoints: elevated outward view showing the full castle silhouette
oblique side view that preserves the main tower and ridge relationship
closer architectural view for masonry and gate/tower verification

facts.observation: The castle is on the Sonnenberg above Annweiler.
The castle is presented as sandstone architecture on a rock ridge.
The ring wall, gate way, fountain tower, main tower and palas base are part of the recognizable current complex.
The current appearance is the result of changing phases of construction, decline and reconstruction, including historicizing additions.
Rooflines and smaller façade details must be read from the approved visual references rather than generalized from a medieval-castle prompt.

signatureFeatures: dominant main tower rising above the compact complex
ring-wall, gate-way and subordinate tower masses
current reconstructed and historicizing appearance rather than an untouched medieval ruin
mustNotInvent: additional towers or a different castle silhouette
generic pointed roofs or fantasy battlements not visible in approved references
invented windows, façades, bridges, banners, coats of arms or operator logos
a flat-ground castle without the elevated rock/forest relationship
a historically pure medieval appearance that hides the documented reconstruction history
